clue.text: In essence, almost keen to hold Blair back

indicators.note: to hold means one piece wraps around the other here
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: back means the name is read from right to left

parts.note: Tony Blair, the former British Prime Minister, supplies his first name

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark about being eager to restrain the former Prime Minister Tony Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In essence' reads as a phrase, but 'In' is only a link; the definition is 'essence'. 'almost', 'back' and 'to hold' each act on the piece beside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A keynote is the central theme or underlying spirit of something, its core idea.

clue.text: Hawkins managed to conceal a relation

indicators.note: to conceal says the letters are tucked away inside the run of words Hawkins managed

explanation.surface: Someone called Hawkins succeeded in keeping a family member out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman is a male blood relative, a member of one's family.

clue.text: Sherry OK? I prepared this pudding

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are made up into a new arrangement, as a dish is prepared

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether sherry is acceptable in the dessert being made.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'this pudding' points back to the clue as an &lit-style flourish; the Yorkshire pudding is a classic British batter accompaniment to roast beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire pudding is a traditional British baked batter dish served with roast beef.

clue.text: The last one: love game, perhaps

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of the following word are rearranged into another possibility

explanation.surface: A tennis remark that a love game might be the final one of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the last of a series.

clue.text: Climbing aboard to take me up to part of London

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before the turn
Barking is a district of east London

explanation.surface: Getting on a vehicle so as to carry oneself towards a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ME into EM; BARKING is an area of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarking means boarding a ship or other vessel, so climbing aboard is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Crumpled dollar bill had influence

parts.note: buck is slang for a dollar
led means guided or had influence over, past tense of lead

explanation.surface: A creased banknote turned out to be persuasive.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckled means bent or collapsed out of shape, much as something crumpled has given way.

clue.text: Dull beginner divides the orchestra

indicators.note: divides means the letter splits the other word in two by going inside it

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, an orchestra
L is a learner driver, a beginner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A tedious novice musician is splitting the orchestra into factions.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland describes something flavourless or uninteresting, which is to say dull.

clue.text: Problem for sister cutting up fish with alcohol

indicators.note: cutting up says one piece slices into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: cod is a fish
a nun is a religious sister
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A nun faces a dilemma while preparing fish with a splash of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzling question or difficult problem.

clue.text: Grasp left ear and tip of nose

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: tip of means only the initial letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: An instruction to take hold of someone's left ear and the end of their nose.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to grasp it mentally, to come to understand it.

clue.text: Broadcasters make brief adjustment with eyes turned

indicators.note: turned means the letters are churned around into a new order

parts.note: adj. is a short form of adjustment

explanation.surface: Radio presenters make a quick tweak while glancing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make brief' asks for the abbreviation of adjustment, ADJ; 'turned' rearranges ADJ with EYES.
explanation.definitionFit: Deejays are disc jockeys, people who present music programmes on air.

clue.text: Child minder to hurry back to Kent

indicators.note: back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to run is to hurry
Kent is in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A babysitter dashes home to the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RUN into NUR; Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse, as in a nursemaid, is employed to look after young children.

clue.text: Bright idea gets supporter in flap

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
taken as written
to wave is to flap, as of a flag

explanation.surface: A clever thought arises from a fan getting agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever thought, an inspired idea.

clue.text: Samantha turns religious and is butchered

indicators.note: turns means the short name is read backwards

parts.note: Sam is short for Samantha
sacred means holy or religious

explanation.surface: A woman named Samantha gets religion and meets a violent end.
explanation.definitionFit: To massacre is to slaughter brutally, so massacred means butchered.

clue.text: Direction taken by Karenina, one of the family

parts.note: N for north is a compass direction
Anna Karenina is the heroine of Tolstoy's novel

explanation.surface: A compass bearing followed by Tolstoy's tragic heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanna is a familiar name for a grandmother, a family member.

clue.text: First person to be covered in scent, leading to a row

indicators.note: to be covered in means the letter is wrapped inside the other word

parts.note: nose is the aroma or bouquet of a wine, its scent
I is the first-person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone drenched in perfume starts an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is loud sound, and a row is a din or racket.

clue.text: Indulgent, despite a piece of cake vanishing

parts.note: a piece of cake is idiomatic for something easy
going means disappearing, vanishing

explanation.surface: A lenient remark made though a slice of cake has disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Easygoing means relaxed and tolerant, so lenient or indulgent.

clue.text: Fantastic or amusing fool

indicators.note: fantastic suggests the letters are wildly reshaped into something else

explanation.surface: A clown is described as wonderfully entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, a fool.

clue.text: Improbable? No fear!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of emphatic refusal, as in certainly not

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both unlikely and, as an exclamation, a firm refusal.

clue.text: Unsettled, if coming with a grandee?

indicators.note: unsettled means the letters are disturbed and moved about

explanation.surface: Someone uneasy about whether an aristocrat will be arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifico was a Venetian nobleman, hence any grandee or person of high rank.

clue.text: Supervision is a mistake

definitions.meaning: an error made by failing to notice something

explanation.surface: A pun on management control and careless error.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both overseeing something and an unintended omission or error.

clue.text: Disgusting old boy seen on "Panorama"

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil
a panorama is a wide view, a scene

explanation.surface: A former pupil appears on the BBC current affairs programme Panorama.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is a long-running BBC investigative TV programme, hence the quotation marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive or repugnant, synonyms of disgusting.

clue.text: Wealthy person, terribly glum when pocketing nothing

indicators.note: pocketing means taking a piece inside, as into a pocket
terribly signals the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A rich man looks gloomy when he earns nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges GLUM to MGUL, and 'when pocketing' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful, rich magnate in business.

clue.text: Support a colleague by rights

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
an ally is a partner or colleague

explanation.surface: Backing a coworker on principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally means according to law, so by rights.

clue.text: Fraud: it's contrary and no good

indicators.note: contrary means turned the opposite way, so read backwards

parts.note: the letters of it's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone insists a deception is both perverse and worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is a confidence trick or swindle, a fraud.

clue.text: A picture of, say, a friend in Calais is held up

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means the run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
ami is French for friend, Calais being a French port

explanation.surface: An image of a French friend being delayed in Calais.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: Dashing crooner keeps entertaining

indicators.note: keeps means one name holds another piece inside it

parts.note: Bing Crosby was a famous crooner
light, as in light entertainment, means undemanding and diverting

explanation.surface: A stylish singer continues to amuse his audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing hopes is blighting them: both mean ruining or frustrating.

clue.text: Keep a piece of timber

definitions.meaning: meals and lodging, as in your keep

explanation.definitionFit: Board is food and lodging (one's keep) and also a sawn plank of wood.

clue.text: Sleep here and half hope to telephone

indicators.note: half means only the first two letters of the four-letter word are kept

explanation.surface: A suggestion to rest somewhere, with half an eye on calling ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a place where travellers stay overnight, so where one sleeps.

clue.text: Get rid of cat in time to go west

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: in means the animal is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: to go west is an idiom for to die
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim suggestion that it is time for the cat to be sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go west' is an idiom meaning to die, not a direction for a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out completely, to get rid of.

clue.text: Cloth for type of shirt worn by Shakespeare

parts.note: T as in T-shirt
Will is William Shakespeare's first name

explanation.surface: A fabric for a garment the Bard might have worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a woven fabric with diagonal ribbing, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Became known by associating me with greed improperly

indicators.note: improperly means the letters are set out wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A reputation emerges by linking oneself to avarice.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerged means came out or became apparent, so became known.

clue.text: Like a lemon chicken, yummy at either end

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, as does chicken

indicators.note: at either end means taking the letter found at an end of the word; both ends are the same letter

explanation.surface: Lemon chicken that is delicious from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yummy' begins and ends with Y, so either end gives the one Y needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowy means somewhat yellow, the colour of a lemon.
